Exact moments of order statistics

Source: R/os_moments.R
os_moments.Rd

Computes the means \(\alpha_i = E[X_{(r_i)}]\), the variances and the covariance matrix \(B_{ij} = \mathrm{Cov}(X_{(r_i)}, X_{(r_j)})\) of the order statistics \(X_{(1)} \le \dots \le X_{(n)}\) of an i.i.d. sample of size n from a continuous distribution, at the ranks ranks, by numerical evaluation of the exact integrals, or from a closed form where the family has one.

Usage

os_moments(
  n,
  ranks = seq_len(n),
  dist = "norm",
  location = 0,
  scale = 1,
  cov = TRUE,
  method = c("auto", "integrate", "closed"),
  rel.tol = 1e-11,
  check = TRUE
)

Arguments

n

The sample size, an integer \(\ge 1\).

ranks

The ranks, strictly increasing integers in \(1, \dots, n\). The default is every rank, which gives the full covariance matrix.

dist

The distribution: one of "norm", "unif", "exp", "logis", "gumbel", or an object made by os_dist. See Details for the standard members.

location, scale

The location and scale applied to the standard member: \(X = \mathrm{location} + \mathrm{scale} \cdot Z\), with scale > 0. The means become \(\mathrm{location} + \mathrm{scale}\,\alpha\) and the covariances \(\mathrm{scale}^2 B\).

cov

TRUE for the full covariance matrix, FALSE for the means and the variances only, which need single integrals and no double integral.

method

"auto" takes the closed form where the family has one and the quadrature elsewhere, "integrate" forces the quadrature, "closed" requires a closed form for every requested quantity and stops otherwise.

rel.tol

The relative tolerance of the quadrature. The single integrals and the inner integral of a product moment run at rel.tol, the outer integral at 100 * rel.tol.

check

Whether to run the run-time checks of the Details and warn when a residual exceeds \(10^{-6}\).

Value

An object of class "osmoments", a list with the components n, ranks, alpha (the means, named by rank), var (the variances), B (the covariance matrix, NULL when cov = FALSE), quad_err (the summed error estimates of the quadrature, see Details), standard (a list with the alpha, var and B of the standard member, before location and scale are applied, which os_blue reads), dist (the os_dist object), location, scale, cov, method, route ("closed", "integrate" or "mixed"), checks (the residuals of the run-time checks, NA where a check did not apply) and call.

Details

The integrals. With cdf \(F\), density \(f\) and \(y < z\), $$f_{r:n}(x) = \frac{n!}{(r-1)!\,(n-r)!} F(x)^{r-1} \{1 - F(x)\}^{n-r} f(x),$$ $$f_{r,s:n}(y, z) = \frac{n!}{(r-1)!\,(s-r-1)!\,(n-s)!} F(y)^{r-1} \{F(z) - F(y)\}^{s-r-1} \{1 - F(z)\}^{n-s} f(y) f(z),$$ and the moments are $$\mu_{r:n} = \int x f_{r:n}(x)\,dx, \qquad \mu^{(2)}_{r:n} = \int x^2 f_{r:n}(x)\,dx, \qquad \mu_{r,s:n} = \int\!\!\int_{y < z} y z f_{r,s:n}(y, z)\,dy\,dz,$$ with \(B_{ij} = \mu_{r_i, r_j:n} - \alpha_i \alpha_j\). The integrals are evaluated by adaptive quadrature (integrate) with four devices: the integrands on the log scale, so that the powers of the tails never underflow; \(\log\{F(z) - F(y)\}\) formed on the smaller tail, so that nothing cancels; the range split at the spike of the order statistic's density, at \(c_r \pm h_r\) with \(c_r = Q(p_r)\), \(p_r = r/(n+1)\) and \(h_r = 10 s_r / f(c_r) + 4\tilde\sigma/\sqrt{n+1}\), \(s_r = \sqrt{p_r(1-p_r)/(n+2)}\), so that the adaptive rule sees the narrow peak at large \(n\) at the end of a piece rather than between its nodes, the outer range of a product moment being split at the points of both ranks; and integration in standardized units of the standard member, \(t = \{x - Q(1/2)\}/\tilde\sigma\), where \(\tilde\sigma\) is the spread of the distribution, its interquartile range divided by that of the standard normal (so \(\tilde\sigma = 1\) for the normal), with each moment taken about its own order statistic's location \(c_r\). The scaling puts the split floor and the integrator's absolute tolerances in the distribution's own units, so that a distribution supplied on any scale is computed as accurately as on the scale one. The centering at \(c_r\) keeps a variance from being the small difference of two moments of size \((c_r - c)^2\): taken about the median \(c\), the variance of the uniform minimum kept seven digits at \(n = 1000\) and none at \(n = 10^5\).

The standard members and the closed forms. "norm" is \(N(0, 1)\); "unif" is the uniform on \([0, 1]\), so that location is the lower end and scale the length; "exp" has unit rate, so that scale is \(1/\mathrm{rate}\); "logis" is the standard logistic; "gumbel" is the standard Gumbel in the maximum form, \(F(x) = \exp(-e^{-x})\). The uniform and the exponential have closed forms for every moment, the logistic for the means and variances, the Gumbel for the mean and variance of the maximum. With method = "auto" these are returned and the rest is quadrature.

The moment condition. A moment is computed only if it exists: with the tail indices \((\nu_L, \nu_U)\) of the distribution, \(E|X_{(r)}|^2 < \infty\) if and only if \(\nu_L r > 2\) and \(\nu_U (n - r + 1) > 2\), and a rank that fails stops the computation with an error. The built-in families always pass.

The error estimate. quad_err is the sum of the error estimates that integrate() reports for the single integrals and for the outer integrals of the product moments, in the units of the standard member before location and scale are applied. It is an estimate, not a bound: the inner integral's estimate is not carried into the outer one, and the errors of the means are not propagated into the covariances. The accuracy evidence is the agreement with the closed forms, the identities and the printed tables, documented in the package's tests.

Accuracy at large n. With method = "integrate", the means and the variances of the uniform and the exponential at the minimum, the quartiles, the median and the maximum agree with their closed forms to within \(10^{-9}\) in relative terms at \(n = 10^4\), \(10^5\) and \(10^6\), and so does the correlation of every pair of them, in absolute terms. Up to the relative errors of the two variances, the relative error of a covariance is the error of its correlation divided by the correlation, so the covariance of two nearly independent order statistics keeps fewer digits: the two extremes, whose correlation is of order \(1/n\), keep five to ten significant digits of their covariance at those sizes, depending on the parent and on \(n\). The package's tests assert the variances and the covariances of adjacent ranks at \(10^{-9}\) and the extremes' covariance at \(10^{-3}\) beyond \(n = 10^4\). A parent as heavy-tailed as the lognormal with log-SD 2 is accurate to about \(10^{-9}\) in relative terms rather than \(10^{-11}\), because the far tail of the inner integral of a covariance is resolved at a fixed tolerance. These are the cases that were measured, not a bound for every parent.

What stops with an error. The quadrature follows the peak of each order statistic's density and the tails of the parent. It does not follow a second mode: for a mixture of two narrow normals, the mode that holds a tenth of the mass fell between the nodes, and the moments came back as those of the other mode. The package therefore integrates the density of every order statistic it computes by quadrature and stops when the mass is not 1 within \(10^{-7}\), naming the rank and the mass it found. It also stops when a piece of the range cannot be resolved, which happens for a moment that does not exist when the tail indices were not declared, for a tail as heavy as a lognormal with log-SD 3 or a Weibull with shape 0.3, for the extremes of a parent whose density is infinite at an endpoint of its support once they concentrate against that endpoint (the minimum of a beta(1/2, 1/2) is computed to \(n = 100\) and refused from \(n = 1000\) on), and for a variance that comes out zero or negative. A wrong number is never returned knowingly, but these checks detect some failures and certify none.

The run-time checks. For a symmetric distribution and a rank set closed under \(r \mapsto n + 1 - r\), the means are antisymmetric and the second moments symmetric about the median, which the integrators do not impose; the product moments are then computed for the pairs with \(r + s \le n + 1\) only and reflected. For a complete rank set, the order statistics are a permutation of the sample, so \(\sum_r \alpha_r = n E[X]\), \(\sum_r \mu^{(2)}_{r:n} = n E[X^2]\) and \(\sum_{r,s} B_{rs} = n\,\mathrm{Var}(X)\) for any parent with a finite second moment, and for the normal parent (recognized by its functions pnorm, dnorm and qnorm, not by its name) every row of \(B\) sums to \(\sigma^2\) as well. The residuals are stored in checks, in the standardized units of the integration (the standard member centered at its median and scaled by its spread, so that the threshold means the same on every scale), and a residual above \(10^{-6}\) raises a warning, as does a covariance matrix with a negative eigenvalue beyond rounding. The checks detect some failures of the quadrature and do not certify its accuracy: a failure that every integral shares, such as a peak missed in the same way at every rank, can satisfy them.

Cost. A single integral takes a fraction of a millisecond and a double integral a few hundredths of a second. When the covariances are not closed forms, a full matrix needs one double integral per pair, \(n(n-1)/2\) of them, halved for a symmetric family.

References

Wu, Z. and Tong, T. (2026). osmoments: Exact means, variances and covariances of order statistics in R. Manuscript. The computation, its verification and the comparison with other software.

Royston, J. P. (1982). Algorithm AS 177: Expected normal order statistics (exact and approximate). Applied Statistics, 31(2), 161-165.

Examples

m <- os_moments(5)            # all ranks of n = 5, standard normal
m$alpha
#>            r1            r2            r3            r4            r5 
#> -1.162964e+00 -4.950190e-01  5.413025e-29  4.950190e-01  1.162964e+00 
m$B
#>            r1        r2        r3        r4         r5
#> r1 0.44753407 0.2243310 0.1481477 0.1057720 0.07421527
#> r2 0.22433096 0.3115190 0.2084354 0.1499427 0.10577198
#> r3 0.14814773 0.2084354 0.2868337 0.2084354 0.14814773
#> r4 0.10577198 0.1499427 0.2084354 0.3115190 0.22433096
#> r5 0.07421527 0.1057720 0.1481477 0.2243310 0.44753407
os_moments(20, ranks = c(1, 5, 10, 20), dist = "exp", scale = 2)
#> Exact moments of order statistics: exp (location 0, scale 2), n = 20, ranks 1 5 10 20
#> alpha (means):
#>        r1        r5       r10       r20 
#> 0.1000000 0.5590213 1.3375430 7.1954790 
#> B (covariance matrix):
#>       r1         r5        r10        r20
#> r1  0.01 0.01000000 0.01000000 0.01000000
#> r5  0.01 0.06289184 0.06289184 0.06289184
#> r10 0.01 0.06289184 0.18558210 0.18558210
#> r20 0.01 0.06289184 0.18558210 6.38465300
#> route: closed; quadrature error estimate: 0
#> checks: reflection n/a; identities n/a
os_moments(100, ranks = c(1, 100), dist = "gumbel", cov = FALSE)
#> Exact moments of order statistics: gumbel (location 0, scale 1), n = 100, ranks 1 100
#> alpha (means):
#>        r1      r100 
#> -1.618284  5.182386 
#> var (variances; cov = FALSE):
#>         r1       r100 
#> 0.05442057 1.64493400 
#> route: mixed; quadrature error estimate: 1.1e-13
#> checks: reflection n/a; identities n/a
